problem:
Consider the matrices

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{1}{3} & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $AB=BA={I}_{2}$
- $AC=CA={I}_{2}$
- $C={A}^{-1}$

feedback.problem:
Consider the matrices

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,C=\frac{1}{15}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $BC=CB={I}_{3}$
- $BD=DB={I}_{3}$
- $D={B}^{-1}$
feedback.worked_solution:
- First, we check whether $BC=CB={I}_{3}.$ Computing $BC$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =\frac{1}{15}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{15} & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne {I}_{3}.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, statement I is false.

- Note, we check whether $BD=DB={I}_{3}.$ Computing $BD$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}BD & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{3}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Likewise, computing $DB$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}DB & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{3}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, statement II is true. As a result, $D={B}^{-1}$ and statement III is true too.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only".
